newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron gunman says he wanted town Jewish forever.
newsitem.headline: Hebron gunman says he wanted town Jewish forever.

text.p: The off-duty Israeli soldier who sprayed bullets at Palestinian shoppers in a Hebron market on Wednesday said he wanted to stop the town from being turned over to the PLO and that the attack was "good" for Israel.

"Abraham bought the Cave of the Patriarchs for 400 shekels of silver. No one will return it," Noam Friedman, triumphantly waving his fist in the air, told Israel's Channel Two television as he was being put into a police van after the attack.
The Bible says that in Hebron some 4,000 years ago Abraham, father of the Jews, paid the substantial sum of 400 shekels of silver for a cave in which to bury his wife Sarah.
Friedman told investigators he wanted to sabotage the handover of the town to Palestinian self-rule, Israel's central area commander Major-General Uzi Dayan told army radio.

The 19-year-old off-duty soldier from Maaleh Adumim settlement near Jerusalem wounded seven Palestinians, two critically, when he indiscriminately fired his M-16 rifle into a vegetable market on Hebron's central Martyr's Street.

Friedman told Israel's Channel One television that he did not regret the attack. Asked how he could justify shooting innocent women and children, Friedman said: "They're not innocent. They hate Israel."
The gunman said the Israeli army gave him the weapon and insisted the attack was "good for the state".
"Hebron is ours now and forever," he told the television.

Channel One said Friedman had been serving for the last six months as an army janitor and had a history of psychiatric problems. Asked by the television whether he thought he was "normal", Friedman replied: "absolutely normal".

The television broadcast pictures of police leaving the Friedman home in Maaleh Adumim carrying several plastic bags it said contained pistol and rifle bullets. The police were not immediately available for comment.

The Cave of the Patriarchs -- the traditional burial place of the biblical fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and their wives -- is one reason Hebron's 400 Jews say they can lay claim to the town of 100,000 Arabs occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
The shooting underscored the fragility of the U.S.-sponsored Middle East peace process and the feeling of betrayal of right-wing Jews opposed to returning captured land to Arabs.

"Bibi remains alone without Jews behind him," Friedman said, using the nickname of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is struggling to seal a deal with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to hand over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO control.
Hebron is the last of seven West Bank towns due to be handed over to Palestinian self-rule under a 1995 Israeli-PLO interim self-rule peace accord.
It was another religious Jew, Yigal Amir, who tried to stop land-for-peace deals by assassinating then-prime minister Yitzhak Rabin 14 months ago.

The Cave of the Patriarchs is also a holy site to Moslems, who call it the Haram al-Ibrahimi. In February 1994 Baruch Goldstein, a Jew from the nearby Kiryat Arba settlement, massacred 29 Palestinians kneeling in prayer at al-Ibrahimi mosque before survivors beat him to death.
